description: In this Next.js 15 App Router inventory management dashboard, implement client/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx so that it fetches the dashboard summary from GET /dashboard/summary using the existing apiRequest helper (@/lib/api-client) on mount, shows a loading state until the data arrives, and then renders: KPI cards for Budget, TotalCustomers, TasksProgress, and TotalProfit (components already exist under client/src/components/dashboard/overview/); Sales and Traffic charts; and LatestProducts/LatestOrders tables. The response may omit recentProducts or recentTransactions — the page must not crash in that case (default to an empty list).

Implement Express middleware exports.protect = (roles = []) => (req, res, next) => {...} in backend/middleware/authMiddleware.js. It must read a Bearer token from the Authorization header, reject with 401 if the header is missing, if the token is malformed/garbage, if it was signed with a different secret than process.env.JWT_SECRET, or if it is expired. On a valid token, it must attach the decoded payload to req.user and call next(). If roles is a non-empty array, it must additionally reject with 403 when req.user's role is not included in roles, while still calling next() when it is (or when roles is empty, meaning no restriction).

Implement run_forecast(sku_input) in ai-module/forecast.py. It connects to MySQL (via mysql.connector, reading sale_date/quantity_sold from sales_history for the given, whitespace-trimmed SKU as a parameterized query), returns {'error': ...} if there is no historical data for that SKU or if the DB connection fails (never raises), and otherwise engineers lag/rolling-average features, trains a RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42), and produces a recursive 365-day forecast aggregated into daily (7 rows), weekly (<=4 rows), monthly (<=12 rows), and yearly (>=1 row) buckets, alongside sku, accuracy, and today fields.

Add exports.getProductsByFilter(req, res) to backend/controllers/inventoryController.js, intended for GET /api/inventory/filter. Read category_id, min_price, max_price, search, page (default 1), and limit (default 10) from req.query. Apply each provided filter with AND semantics (category_id exact match, min_price/max_price as inclusive bounds on unit_price, search as a wildcarded LIKE match against product name and SKU), paginate with LIMIT/OFFSET, and return { data: [...rows], meta: { totalItems, currentPage } }. Every filter value must be passed as a bound parameter to db.execute(sql, params); none may be concatenated or interpolated directly into the SQL string.

Add exports.getCategoryForecast(req, res) to backend/controllers/forecastController.js, intended for GET /api/inventory/forecast/category/:category_id. Look up all products in the given category (SELECT sku, product_name FROM products WHERE category_id = ?, parameterized). If none match, return 200 with { category_id, data: [] } without spawning any forecast process. Otherwise, for each matching product, run the existing ai-module/forecast.py script the same way getProductForecast already does (spawn the venv's python3 on forecast.py <sku>, parse its JSON stdout), and return 200 with { category_id, data: [{ sku, product_name, forecast: {...} }, ...] }. If one product's forecast fails, that product's entry should carry { sku, product_name, error } instead without preventing other products' forecasts from succeeding. A database error on the category lookup itself should return 500.

Add exports.bulkAdjustStock(req, res) to backend/controllers/inventoryController.js. Accept req.body.adjustments as an array of { product_id, quantity_change, reason } objects. Using a single database transaction (db.getConnection(), beginTransaction()), first read the current quantity_on_hand for every affected product_id from the inventory table. Validate that applying every adjustment's quantity_change would not drive any product's quantity_on_hand negative; if any adjustment would, roll back the transaction without applying any adjustment in the batch (not just the offending one) and return 400. Otherwise, for each adjustment: update inventory.quantity_on_hand by quantity_change, and insert an audit row into stock_transactions (product_id, user_id, transaction_type, quantity_changed, reason), where transaction_type is 'Inflow' for a positive quantity_change and 'Outflow' for a negative one, and user_id comes from req.user?.user_id (default to 1 if absent, matching this codebase's existing receivePurchaseOrder pattern). Commit and return 200 on success. On an unexpected database error, roll back and return 500. Always release the connection, even on failure.

Wire up the notification preferences form in client/src/components/dashboard/settings/notifications.tsx, whose onSubmit is currently a no-op (event.preventDefault() only, with uncontrolled checkboxes and no state tracking, and no backend call). Convert the 4 checkboxes to controlled React state with keys emailProductUpdates, emailSecurityUpdates, phoneProductUpdates, and phoneSecurityUpdates (in that DOM order), initialized to match the current visual defaults (the first checkbox in each column starts checked, the second starts unchecked) — keep the existing visible labels and layout unchanged. On submit, call apiRequest('/users/notification-preferences', { method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(preferences) }) with the current preferences state as the JSON body, matching the apiRequest-call pattern used by every other form in this codebase (e.g. account-details-form.tsx). While the request is in flight, the Save changes button must be disabled, matching the isSaving/isSubmitting convention used by those same forms, and re-enabled once the request settles.

Create ai-module/reorder.py with a function calculate_reorder_point(daily_forecast, lead_time_days, service_level_z=1.65). daily_forecast is a list of dicts shaped like forecast.py's `daily` output: [{"date": ..., "predicted_sales": int}, ...]. Compute average_daily_demand as the mean of predicted_sales across daily_forecast, and the population standard deviation of the same values (demand_stdev). safety_stock = round(service_level_z * demand_stdev * sqrt(lead_time_days)); reorder_point = round(average_daily_demand * lead_time_days) + safety_stock. Return {"average_daily_demand": ..., "safety_stock": ..., "reorder_point": ...}. If daily_forecast is empty or lead_time_days is not positive, return {"error": ...} instead of raising, matching forecast.py's existing failure-handling convention (never raises). The result must be JSON-serializable.

Add exports.getCategorySalesReport(req, res) to backend/controllers/categoryController.js. Query total sales revenue and units sold per category by joining categories to products to sale_order_items (which has product_id, quantity, unit_price), using LEFT JOINs throughout so categories with no sales still appear in the results with zero totals rather than being excluded. Group by category and compute SUM(quantity * unit_price) as total_revenue and SUM(quantity) as total_units_sold per category, matching the GROUP BY/LEFT JOIN convention already used by getAllCategories in the same file. Return 200 with the resulting rows as a bare JSON array (res.status(200).json(rows)), matching getAllCategories' existing response shape (not the {data, meta} pagination wrapper used elsewhere). On a database error, return 500.

Create backend/routes/accountRoute.js, an Express Router exposing GET /session. The route must be protected by the existing exports.protect middleware from backend/middleware/authMiddleware.js, requiring either the 'admin' or 'user' role (protect(['admin', 'user'])). Requests without a valid Authorization Bearer token, or with an invalid/expired one, are rejected by the middleware itself (401) — no explicit handling needed in the route handler. When the request passes the middleware, the route handler must respond with 200 and a JSON body of the shape { user: req.user }, where req.user is the decoded token payload protect() attaches to the request. Export the configured router (module.exports = router).
